definition: DTs refers to digital textbooks: educational materials delivered in digital formats, often with interactive features and easy access through devices, apps, links, or QR codes. In this source, they are discussed as tools designed to match learners’ information-processing styles and support timely, personalized learning.

reasons: The definition claims DTs are “designed to match learners’ information-processing styles,” but the provided packet only mentions “information processing methods” and does not substantiate a “information-processing styles” framing as stated.

The definition is not strictly limited to what the packet describes as “future direction” and “should be developed,” yet it presents the intent (“tools designed to match…,” “support timely, personalized learning”) as a more general description rather than the packet’s scoped findings and recommendations.

The definition broadens the source too far by presenting DTs as a general category of educational materials; the packet only supports DTs as digital textbooks discussed in undergraduate nursing education.
The field label ‘development’ is not clearly supported by the packet’s content, which is about nursing education and digital textbooks rather than a development sense in psychology/counselling.
